business_problem: Cuhaci Peterson needed to let designers collaborate across offices and remote locations without shipping large Revit and AutoCAD workloads to local workstations, but fragmented on-prem file servers and geography-constrained hiring were blocking both continuity and growth.
solution_summary: Cuhaci Peterson standardized its design environment on Azure Virtual Desktop backed by NVIDIA virtual GPU infrastructure so Revit and AutoCAD workloads no longer depend on high-end workstations sitting in specific offices. The company runs NVadsA10v5 virtual machines with NVIDIA A10 GPUs and RTX Virtual Workstation capabilities in a shared host-pool model, giving designers in the United States and India access to the same applications, files, and performance profile through one cloud workspace. Centralized images and file services let IT update environments once instead of machine by machine, while the GPU-backed VDI model keeps graphics-heavy sessions responsive for 12 to 13 users per VM. That architecture turned virtual desktops into an operating model for round-the-clock production, broader recruiting, and simpler office expansion rather than just a remote-work contingency.

solution_components.name: NVIDIA vGPU
solution_components.role: Virtualizes GPU capacity so design applications can be delivered through cloud desktops instead of local towers.

solution_components.name: NVIDIA RTX Virtual Workstation
solution_components.role: Provides the graphics-acceleration profile needed for Revit and AutoCAD in the virtual desktop environment.

solution_components.name: NVIDIA A10 GPUs
solution_components.role: Power the NVadsA10v5 virtual machines that host multi-user design sessions.

solution_components.name: Azure Virtual Desktop
solution_components.role: Delivers the shared cloud desktop environment designers use from the US and India.

data_flow: Project files and application images are centralized in the Azure host pool, where designers connect through Azure Virtual Desktop to NVIDIA A10-backed sessions. Revit and AutoCAD workloads are rendered through RTX Virtual Workstation and vGPU, and the resulting changes stay inside the shared environment for cross-office handoffs and IT management.
business_outcome: Cuhaci Peterson removed geography as a hiring constraint, enabled 24/7 US-India production handoffs, simplified IT operations with standardized desktops, and reduced hardware and licensing costs through long-term reserved NVIDIA GPU-powered virtual machines.
architecture_clues: The environment uses NVadsA10v5-series VMs with 36 cores and 880 GB of RAM
